rmix-01-c1.text: Plutarch (trans. John Thomson, ed. William W. Goodwin) (1874). De fraterno amore (Of Brotherly Love), in Plutarch's Morals, Vol. III. Perseus Digital Library, Tufts University.
rmix-01-c1.quote: And that was it which they commonly called Syncretism.
rmix-01-c1.claim: Plutarch used the Greek synkretismos for the Cretans, who quarreled among themselves but closed ranks against outside enemies

rmix-04-c3.text: Kennedy. Church of the Lukumi Babalu Aye v. City of Hialeah, 508 U.S. 520. law.cornell.edu.
rmix-04-c3.quote: The Free Exercise Clause commits government itself to religious tolerance

rmix-02-c1.quote: An entity called Cao Dai (literally, "high tower," a Daoist epithet for the supreme god) appeared and delivered to the group the fundamental features of the religion
rmix-02-c1.claim: That being was called Cao Đài, "High Tower" or "High Palace," a reverent title for God.

rmix-02-c2.quote: Its elaborate organizational structure, headed by a pope, cardinals, and archbishops, was patently inspired by Roman Catholicism.
rmix-02-c2.claim: The hierarchy borrows the shape of the Catholic Church, with a pope, cardinals, bishops and priests

rmix-03-c3.quote: Scholars (and practitioners) prefer the spelling vodou because of the negative stereotypes attached to the Americanized spelling voodoo
rmix-03-c3.claim: Scholars and practitioners prefer the spelling "Vodou" partly to separate the religion from the Hollywood word.

rmix-05-c1.claim: Ras Tafari Makonnen was crowned Emperor Haile Selassie I of Ethiopia

rmix-06-c2.text: 400,000 say beliefs are 'Jedi'. The Irish Times.
rmix-06-c2.quote: Over 390,000 people wrote Jedi under "any other religion" on their 2001 census form, more than those who registered their faith as Jewish, Buddhist or Sikh
rmix-06-c2.claim: On census day 390,127 people, almost 0.8 percent of the population, declared themselves Jedi, more than gave Judaism or Buddhism.
